explanation: To solve a system by graphing, draw both lines and find where they cross: that single point is the (x, y) that makes BOTH equations true at once. The tracer dots ride each line, and the dashed guides drop from the crossing to show its coordinates. Give the lines different slopes for exactly one solution; equal slopes make them parallel (no solution) or the same line (infinitely many solutions).
bullets: The solution is the point that lies on both lines at the same time.
Different slopes -> exactly one crossing; the dashed lines read off its coordinates.
Equal slopes -> parallel (no solution) or identical (infinitely many).
